bio: Tonga's only national forest park, a band of rainforest on ʻEua's east coast edged by cliffs and caves.
A 4.5 km² rainforest park on ʻEua's east side, home to the Big Ovava Tree and trails above sea cliffs.
Tonga's only forest national park, with hiking trails through rainforest above cliffs, caves and chasms.
Stonehenge-like rock shapes on 200 m cliffs, with wild horses grazing between them and seabirds below.
Sculpted rocks scattered over grassy clifftop terraces, where brown boobies and frigatebirds glide past.
Wild horses roam among rock formations on tall cliffs, with nesting seabirds curious about visitors.
A cliff-edge lookout over the open ocean, on the same road south as Haʻaluma Beach and the Rock Gardens.
Cliffs on ʻEua's rocky south shore, a short viewpoint stop on the road out to Haʻaluma Beach.
A cliff viewpoint in ʻEua's far south, reached on the way past Haʻaluma Beach to the clifftop rocks.
A giant ovava (banyan) in ʻEua's rainforest, said to be over 800 years old, reached by a bush walk.
An ovava tree thought to be more than 800 years old, the main attraction of ʻEua National Park.
Ancient banyan deep in ʻEua's forest park, on a trail that starts near Hafu Pool.
A large natural stone bridge by the sea on ʻEua, named for the demigod Maui.
A natural stone arch on ʻEua's shore, named for the legendary Maui, and one of the island's highlights.
Tremendous natural rock archway beside the sea, named in Tongan legend for Maui.
A long white beach on ʻEua's south coast, good for snorkelling in its tidal pools and for swimming.
White sand backed by green forest, with large tidal pools full of tropical fish for snorkelling.
Southern ʻEua's swimming beach, reached down an access road best walked, with snorkelling in tidal pools.
Coral reef at sea level along the shore between ʻOhonua and Tufuvai, dotted with small tidal pools.
A strip of near-sea-level coral reef between ʻOhonua and Tufuvai, holding many small ʻotumatafena pools.
Small tidal pools in a flat coral shore, a feature unique to ʻEua, between ʻOhonua and Tufuvai.
A scuba dive into a cavern about 100 m long, entered at 28 m, with light pouring through holes in its roof.
An underwater cavern found around 2001, 100 m long and 30 m deep, lit by shafts of light from above.
Guided dive into a huge sea cave beside ʻEua's cliff, passing sharks and groupers on the way out.
